Cornetist Ed Polcer is an active advocate for American jazz. He was born in Paterson, NJ on February 10, 1937 and was able to visit the thriving club scene of New York City as a youth where he heard numerous jazz legends. He attended Princeton University and joined Stan Rubin’s Tigertown Five. Ed has been at the forefront of presenting informative and entertaining productions to new jazz audiences, including “A Night At Eddie Condon’s” and “The Magic of Swing Street.” He was the manager of Eddie Condon’s in New York from 1975 until 1985, and has served as President of the International Art of Jazz. An active traveler and performer, Ed may be seen at many of the jazz parties and festivals across the country.
Ed was interviewed in Tarrytown, New York on October 31, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
